home_about_body_1: Lil SBD is an uptempo hardcore producer from eastern France, building tracks around sharp zaag kicks, pressure that keeps moving forward, and just enough control to make the impact land harder.
home_about_body_2: The goal is simple: make hard music that still feels like music. Heavy enough for a late set, but not built like disposable noise that is loud for ten seconds and empty right after.
home_about_description: A short introduction to the project, the sound, and the direction behind it.
home_contact_description: For bookings, collabs, questions, or course interest, email is the cleanest point of contact. The socials are here if you just want to keep up with the project.
home_course_body: The course is free and aimed first at hard music producers, but the workflow translates well to anyone making EDM. It covers kicks, sound design, mixing, samples, and the decisions that make a track actually hit instead of just clipping harder.
home_course_description: A practical course for people who want real production process, not generic advice.
home_course_item_1: Kick building from simple starts to usable results
home_course_item_2: Sound design for harder drops, leads, and textures
home_course_item_3: Mixing choices that keep aggression clean and focused
home_course_item_4: Samples, workflow, and what actually matters in the session
home_course_note_body_1: It is built for hard music first, but producers from other EDM styles will still get value out of the sound design, kick work, and mixing logic.
home_course_note_body_2: It stays focused on production. No artist-growth filler, no vague mindset talk, just the technical side and the choices behind the sound.
home_course_note_description: Clear on who it is for and what it actually covers.
home_course_title: A free course for hard music producers
home_faq_1_answer: Fast, heavy uptempo hardcore with zaag kicks, but without dropping the parts that make a track feel alive. The aim is impact with tension, structure, and actual intent behind it.
home_faq_1_question: What kind of sound is Lil SBD after?
home_faq_2_answer: No. It is built from a hard-music perspective, but most of the kick work, sound design, sample choices, and mixing ideas still apply across EDM.
home_faq_2_question: Is the course only for uptempo producers?
home_faq_3_answer: Yes. Use the email below if you want the most direct route for bookings, collabs, or questions. The socials are there for the rest.
home_faq_description: The obvious questions people tend to have before they decide to stay, listen, or reach out.
home_feature_1_description: Hard kicks and aggressive energy, but arranged so the track still has movement and shape.
home_feature_2_description: The project leans into weight, tension, and identity instead of empty loudness for its own sake.
home_feature_3_description: A free course gives producers a serious way into the same process without turning the site into a sales funnel.
home_focus_description: The project is built around a few things that matter more than trend chasing.
home_focus_item_1: Uptempo hardcore where the kicks serve the track instead of swallowing it whole
home_focus_item_2: Energy made for late sets, not for sitting quietly in the background
home_focus_item_3: A stronger musical backbone under the aggression
home_focus_item_4: A free resource for producers who care about technique
